thread:
Alex S.: Heads-up — customers reporting sudden p95/p99 spikes on tool/function-calling flows starting ~09:15 UTC. Multiple orgs see p99 jump from ~600ms to ~2.4s, errors are rare but timeouts increased. Request ids: req_9a3f, req_b12c. Anyone on this?

Priya N.: @Marco G. @Olivia R. can you pull the route-level latency breakdowns? Do we see router vs validation vs model time? :eyes:

Marco G.: Looking now. Quick summary: around 09:14 we rolled change to tool-router that enabled per-tool JSON-schema validation on server side for structured outputs (opt-in flag got enabled for some customers accidentally). Metrics show an increased CPU spike on router hosts and higher tail latency. Preliminary flame: router->json_validate step adds ~700–900ms on p99 for large tool outputs.

Olivia R.: Confirming — the change was meant to be gated, but a config propagation bug flipped it for a small subset of tenants. Validation uses ajv with full schema deref for nested objects; worst-case output size >50kb triggers expensive checks.

Dana L.: Customer impact: multiple PLG customers saw slow responses in chat flows that call tools. One escalated to support and is asking for a rollback. What are mitigations we can apply quickly?

Marco G.: Short term: 1) disable server-side validation globally for tool outputs (kill switch) 2) add size guard: skip validation if output > 8kb 3) route affected tenants to dedicated router without validation. I can push the disable now.

Priya N.: Please outline rollback steps and expected timing. Also need a postmortem plan and communication draft for affected customers.

Marco G.: Rollback plan: patch the feature-flag system and flip validation=false for all tenants, deploy to router fleet (rolling, priority zone first). Expected time: ~12 minutes to flip + 10–15 minutes for servers to drain. I'll kick it off.

deploy-bot: CI pipeline started for rollback patch (build 2026.03.17-678). Deploy to routers in us-central-1 first.

Alex S.: Noted. I'll message the two primary customers and flag support tickets. Any interim client-side workarounds we can ask them to try? e.g., request smaller tool outputs or increase client timeout?

Olivia R.: Ask them to pin model to prior router variant (if available) or reduce tool output verbosity — but that's rough. We'll aim for rollback ASAP. Also we should capture a replay set for repro. Please don't purge logs.

Marco G.: Rollback started. Pushing config flip now.

Priya N.: From observability: after flip at 09:27 UTC we see p99 dropping back from ~2.4s -> ~650ms in affected routes. CPU on router hosts dropping ~35%. Still seeing a small tail at ~900ms for requests with very large tool payloads.

Dana L.: Good. Can we draft customer note: brief root cause, mitigation, ETA for full fix, and ask for any reproduced examples? I'll prepare initial message.

Olivia R.: Next steps for a proper fix: - Move validation off hot path (async validation post-response) OR - apply streaming/partial validation + schema compilation cache per model/tool - Tighten config gating and add integration test for feature-flag propagation - Add size+complexity heuristics to skip validation for deep/nested outputs

Marco G.: Agreed. I'll open a PR for schema compilation cache (use precompiled ajv validators stored per-schema hash) and a follow-up to add server-side size cutoff and async validator queue. Est. 2–3 sprints to get full safe rollout.

Alex S.: Support follow-up: ticket updates posted, customers informed of rollback and temporary mitigation. Will escalate to account execs for the bigger customers.

Priya N.: Add an SLO test to CI that simulates tool outputs with schema validation enabled to catch p99 regressions. Also add an alert when router CPU increases >25% over baseline tied to flag flips.

Dana L.: Thanks all. Please paste PR links and the postmortem draft in this thread when ready. Closing loop once we have customer comms and timeline. :thumbsup:

Marco G.: PRs: (draft) github.com/redwood-inference/routers/pulls/312 (schema-cache) and /pulls/313 (validation-size-cutoff). Postmortem draft coming in ~2 hours.

Alex S.: Closing notes: main root cause = accidental config propagation enabling server-side JSON-schema validation for structured tool outputs; exacerbated by expensive schema dereferencing on large nested outputs. Mitigation = rollback + size guard; long-term = compiled validators, async validation, CI SLOs.

Priya N.: Filing incident now and tagging for postmortem. Thanks team.
